Molecular insights into peptide agonist engagement with the PTH receptor.

Cary BP(1), Gerrard EJ(2), Belousoff MJ(3), Fletcher MM(2), Jiang Y(3), Russell

The parathyroid hormone (PTH) 1 receptor (PTH1R) is a G protein-coupled receptor 
(GPCR) that regulates skeletal development and calcium homeostasis. Here, we 
describe cryo-EM structures of the PTH1R in complex with fragments of the two 
hormones, PTH and PTH-related protein, the drug abaloparatide, as well as the 
engineered tool compounds, long-acting PTH (LA-PTH) and the truncated peptide, 
M-PTH(1-14). We found that the critical N terminus of each agonist engages the 
transmembrane bundle in a topologically similar fashion, reflecting similarities 
in measures of Gαs activation. The full-length peptides induce subtly different 
extracellular domain (ECD) orientations relative to the transmembrane domain. In 
the structure bound to M-PTH, the ECD is unresolved, demonstrating that the ECD 
is highly dynamic when unconstrained by a peptide. High resolutions enabled 
identification of water molecules near peptide and G protein binding sites. Our 
results illuminate the action of orthosteric agonists of the PTH1R.
